## Major Networking Trends

| Trend | Description |
|---|---|
| **Convergence** | Telephone and computer networks have merged into unified platforms — e.g. Microsoft Teams and Zoom combine voice, video, and data on a single network |
| **Broadband** | High-speed internet is now a basic expectation for businesses of all sizes |
| **Wireless (Wi-Fi & 5G)** | Employees work from airports, cafes, or client sites without being tied to office desks |
| **Cloud networking** | AWS and Azure manage infrastructure, reducing costs and increasing scalability automatically |

Together these trends create a more mobile, efficient, and agile ecosystem.

---

## The Internet

The largest and most influential network in the world.

- **ISPs (Internet Service Providers)** — how organisations and individuals connect to the internet
- **IP addresses** — unique identifiers for every device connected to the internet
- **DNS (Domain Name Service)** — translates numeric IP addresses into human-readable names (e.g. nus.edu.sg, amazon.com)
- **Backbone networks** — large network service providers carry traffic between countries and continents

**Governance:** The internet is not centrally owned. It is coordinated by:
- Internet Architecture Board (IAB)
- ICANN
- World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)

This decentralised governance allowed the internet to scale rapidly and support global innovation.

### Internet Structure

Local/regional networks → National backbones → Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) globally

- Thousands of networks communicate using shared protocols like **TCP/IP**
- Resilience: if one node fails, traffic reroutes via another path
- Vulnerability: DNS attacks or routing misconfigurations can still disrupt large portions of traffic

**Example:** A 2016 major DDoS attack on a DNS provider temporarily took down Twitter, Netflix, and Airbnb — showing how even a decentralised system has shared points of risk.

## Cellular Mobile Networks

| Generation | Capability |
|---|---|
| **3G** | Basic browsing and email on the go |
| **4G** | Full-featured mobile apps (e.g. Grab rides, real-time Slack messages) |
| **5G** | Not just speed — powers self-driving cars, remote-control robots, augmented reality field repair tools; connects machines and processors at unprecedented responsiveness |

---

## Wi-Fi

- Allows users to move freely without losing connectivity
- Ideal for open office layouts, campus environments, remote collaboration
- **Example (Singapore):** On a university campus, students transition from lecture halls to libraries to cafes without disconnecting
- In business: supports flexible workspaces, BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) policies, and visitor access

---

## Bluetooth

- Short-range, low-power connections — builds personal area networks
- **In a meeting room:** laptops connect to projectors, speakers pair with microphones, files exchanged without cables
- Powers wearables, wireless headsets, printers, IoT sensors in smart offices
- Key difference from Wi-Fi: **Bluetooth connects devices to each other**, not to a central network
- Use cases: point-of-sale terminals, contactless visitor check-ins

---

## Extended Wireless Ecosystem

| Technology | Use Case |
|---|---|
| **IoT sensors** | Smart thermostats, industrial equipment monitors |
| **Wireless LAN** | Dedicated connectivity for specific organisational needs |
| **RFID** | Contactless identification and tracking — e.g. inventory systems recording items as they move through warehouses |
| **Wireless sensor networks** | Monitor environmental conditions, equipment status, and security parameters |

> Most modern environments blend cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth to meet a variety of communication needs.

## Case: Alibaba's Hema Supermarket App

A real-world example of integrated infrastructure creating business value.

- Mobile apps connect customers to inventory systems
- QR codes bridge physical and digital experiences
- Real-time data analytics optimise operations and personalise offerings
- IoT sensors track inventory and customer movements
- Real-time inventory management prevents stockouts while enabling rapid delivery

**Result:**
- Traditional supermarkets become fulfilment centres
- Shopping becomes a true omnichannel experience
- Data drives continuous improvement
